## Why this course?

Fitting a mechanistic model to outbreak data is a common task in an outbreak response, and a common one in research.

::: {.fragment}
The methods that do it well are scattered across literatures, and it is easy to reach for the wrong one, or the right one badly tuned.
:::

::: {.fragment}
There was no single place that taught them together, with the code to run them.
:::

## Who are we?

The course has been taught at LSHTM for over a decade, by the Centre for the Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases.

::: {.fragment}
It was written by [several people](../../authors.qmd) over that time, and this is the first year it is taught in Julia.
:::

## Who are you?

Around the room:

- your name
- where you have come from
- what you are hoping to fit

## How the course works

Each session opens with a short set of slides and then becomes a practical you work through.

::: {.fragment}
The practicals are the course. Sit with someone and compare answers, and ask us as soon as you are stuck.
:::

::: {.fragment}
Every line of Julia is given complete. The exercises ask you to predict, interpret and choose, never to debug.
:::
